rationale: Jesus' answer to the second request for a sign repeats His answer to the first. In this app's BSB, 16:4 matches 12:39 from "A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign" to "except the sign of"; 12:39 then ends "the prophet Jonah," 16:4 "Jonah." A script over the BSB finds "wicked and adulterous" only in these two verses. In Greek, the sixteen words of 16:4 from genea to Iona are the same sixteen words, in order, as in 12:39, in all nine editions Bible Hub lists (a script comparison; the Greek Orthodox text writes ei me as one word at 12:39). The SBL, Nestle 1904, Westcott-Hort and Tischendorf texts end the clause at Iona in 16:4, while the Byzantine, Greek Orthodox and both Textus Receptus texts add tou prophetou there too, matching 12:39 exactly. A saying repeated within one Gospel is why the type is motif, following conn-matt12-vipers-matt3 and conn-matt13-net-weeds, and the verbatim repetition is why the label is strong. What differs is the setting: at 12:38 the askers are "some of the scribes and Pharisees" and Jesus explains the sign (12:40-42); at 16:1 they are "the Pharisees and Sadducees," the request is for "a sign from heaven," and the Pulpit Commentary notes that here Jesus "does not here explain them." Whether 16:1-4 records a second request or a doubled report of one is a named dispute in the lesson's Positions; the grade is for the repeated wording, which both sides accept. The Jonah background itself is graded in lesson 26 (conn-matt12-sign-jonah1) and is not repeated here.
